about: The UCLMS Toolkit (MBBS0077) is a Year 1 module in UCL's MBBS programme, taught in person in Term 1 and carrying 0 credits. UCL's 2026/27 module catalogue says it aims to help students develop skills for life, as a medical student and beyond, while developing awareness of social, ethical and political responsibility, and that it focuses on citizenship, community, equality and inclusivity. Its assessment is listed as 100% other form of assessment. The catalogue publishes no learning outcomes, syllabus or session list, so this guide explains what is confirmed and how to prepare; it does not invent a syllabus.

notes.h: What the UCLMS Toolkit is, and what UCL has published about it
notes.body:
The UCLMS Toolkit (MBBS0077) is a Year 1 module in UCL's MBBS programme, but it is not a science block with a lecture list. It is a module about skills and responsibilities, and the only official page that describes it in any detail is the module catalogue entry, so this note keeps to what that entry says.

What the 2026/27 catalogue entry says (last updated 10 March 2026)
- Title and code: UCLMS Toolkit, MBBS0077. It is run by UCL Medical School in the Faculty of Medical Sciences and is open only to students on the MBBS programme.
- Level and mode: undergraduate, FHEQ Level 4 (first-year level), taught in person.
- Timing: the intended teaching term is Term 1.
- Credits: 0. No alternative credit options are offered.
- Aims: to help students develop skills for life, as a medical student and beyond, while developing an awareness of social, ethical and political responsibility.
- Themes named in the description: citizenship, being part of a community, and equality and inclusivity, including their potential to have an impact on wider society.
- Assessment: listed as 100% "other form of assessment". The page gives no task, no weighting breakdown and no marking criteria.

What UCL has not published
The catalogue entry has no learning outcomes, no syllabus and no list of sessions or topics. This pack therefore does not invent one. If a revision site or a friend gives you a session-by-session list, treat it as unofficial until you see it on your Year 1 Moodle pages.

What this means for how you approach it
- Expect something different from the systems modules. There is no body of facts to memorise for a written paper in the way you would for Circulation and Breathing.
- The module is about how you work, reflect and behave as a medical student. Engagement and completing whatever tasks are set matter more than last-minute revision.
- A module with 0 credits is still part of the course. It is listed with the other Year 1 modules, and Year 1 progression depends on completing the prescribed course (see the next note).

Exam tips: the Toolkit has no published written exam. Read the task instructions on Moodle as soon as they appear, keep any deadline in your calendar, and do not rely on second-hand descriptions of what the assessment involves.

notes.h: Where the Toolkit fits in Year 1 and how completion is recorded
notes.body:
UCL's Year 1 programme page lists the UCLMS Toolkit among the Year 1 modules, alongside the systems-based modules and the vertical modules that carry the Clinical and Professional Practice themes. This note covers where it sits and how completing it is recorded, using only what the official documents say.

Where it sits
- The Year 1 programme page describes the systems-based teaching as a series of sequential, integrated modules, each based around a physiological system (for example Circulation and Breathing). The Toolkit is not one of these systems-based modules.
- The catalogue gives Term 1 as its intended teaching term. Exact session dates, times and rooms can change, so use your own Year 1 timetable on Moodle rather than any copied list.

How it relates to the Applied Knowledge Tests
Year 1 summative assessment consists of two Applied Knowledge Tests (AKTs), described in UCL's 2026–27 Year 1 Format of Assessments as online integrated papers with single best answer (SBA) and very short answer (VSA) questions, with no negative marking. That document describes the AKTs and the formative papers; it does not mention the Toolkit. The Toolkit's own catalogue entry lists its assessment as "other form of assessment", so do not assume it is examined in an AKT. Check Moodle for what is required.

Progression from Year 1 to Year 2
UCL's 2026–27 MBBS Mark Scheme and Boards of Examiners document sets out the rules for progression:
- Complete the full prescribed course of study and obtain sign-off for all required modules and placements.
- Submit a portfolio containing marks for all required coursework, student selected components and GMC-mandated procedures.
- Fulfil the portfolio and coursework requirements listed on the Year Moodle site.
- Each module must be completed and graded.
The document does not name the Toolkit, and it does not say how a 0-credit module is graded. The Year 1 Moodle site is the place to confirm how Toolkit work is recorded.

Who to ask
The catalogue entry lists a Year 1 team contact address (mbbsy1@ucl.ac.uk) for queries about the module. Your personal tutor and the Year 1 Moodle announcements are other sources.

Exam tips: keep a simple checklist of every Year 1 requirement you are told about (modules, portfolio items, sign-offs) and tick them off during the year, rather than discovering gaps in June.

notes.h: The themes in the catalogue description
notes.body:
The catalogue description of the UCLMS Toolkit is short, but it names several themes. This note explains each in plain terms. The explanations are general background to help you think about the themes; they are not a list of Toolkit sessions, which UCL has not published.

Skills for life
The description says the aim is to help students develop skills for life, as a medical student and beyond. In practice, this points to skills that transfer between contexts, such as working with others, reflecting on your own behaviour and taking responsibility, rather than skills used in only one module.

Social, ethical and political responsibility
The description also refers to developing an awareness of social, ethical and political responsibility. Health and healthcare are shaped by social conditions, laws and policy, and decisions made by clinicians have effects on people and communities. Being aware of this means asking not only what is clinically possible but what is fair, who is affected and who is left out.

Citizenship and community
The catalogue lists the importance of citizenship and of being a part of a community. This can be read at several levels: your cohort and university community, the local communities around your placements and the wider society a doctor serves.

Equality and inclusivity, and their potential impact on wider society
The description names equality and inclusivity and their potential to have an impact on wider society. As general legal background, the Equality Act 2010 (section 4) names nine protected characteristics: age; disability; gender reassignment; marriage and civil partnership; pregnancy and maternity; race; religion or belief; sex; and sexual orientation. Inclusion is wider than the legal list, since people can be disadvantaged by many circumstances, but the Act is a useful reference point for understanding what the law protects.

Questions you can use to prepare
- Where have I seen unequal treatment or exclusion, and what could be done about it?
- How do my own assumptions affect how I listen to colleagues and patients?
- What does being part of a community require of me when I am busy?

Exam tips: because no assessment task is published, practise explaining each theme in a few sentences with one concrete example. That habit helps with whatever reflective or written work the Toolkit sets.

notes.h: Getting the most from the Toolkit
notes.body:
Because UCL's pages give little detail on the Toolkit sessions, you will get the most from the module by using general good habits and checking Moodle for the specifics. The suggestions below are study advice, not UCL requirements.

Before the sessions
- Look at the Year 1 Moodle pages for the Toolkit as soon as they appear: read any instructions, session information, pre-reading and the assessment task, and note deadlines in your calendar.
- Check your Year 1 timetable for the sessions, and note any preparation you are asked to do.
- If anything is unclear (what the assessment is, how it is recorded or how to submit it), email the Year 1 team early using the address given in the catalogue entry, or ask your personal tutor.

During the sessions
- Take brief notes: what you learned, what surprised you, what you would do differently.
- Take part in group discussions. The themes in the description (community, equality, responsibility) depend on hearing views different from your own.
- Record any examples you could use later in a written or reflective task. Write the details down soon after the session while they are fresh.

After the sessions
- Use a simple reflection structure: what happened; what I thought and felt; what I learned; what I will do next. This is a common reflective approach, not a UCL template.
- Keep anything that Moodle says should go in your portfolio, and keep a copy of anything you submit.
- Keep personal or patient information out of reflections unless you are told how to anonymise it.

Making it count
The Toolkit carries 0 credits, so it is easy to treat as lower priority than the systems modules. UCL lists it as one of the Year 1 modules and the Mark Scheme requires that the prescribed course is completed and signed off, so plan time for it.

A note on sources
The catalogue entry was last updated on 10 March 2026. If your Moodle pages say something different from this pack, follow Moodle.

Exam tips: build a short weekly routine for the Toolkit, such as a ten-minute reflection after each session, so that you can write a good submission from your own notes.

questions.q: How does UCL's 2026/27 module catalogue list the assessment of the UCLMS Toolkit (MBBS0077)?
options: A two-hour written examination in Term 1
questions.why: The catalogue entry lists the assessment as 100% 'other form of assessment' and gives no further breakdown. The two Applied Knowledge Tests are the Year 1 summative papers, which are described in the Format of Assessments document and in separate module entries, so they are not the Toolkit's listed assessment. A Term 1 written examination is not mentioned anywhere on the entry. A 50/50 coursework and examination split is a common pattern in other modules, but this entry shows a single 100% category.

questions.q: Where does UCL's 2026–27 Mark Scheme say the portfolio and coursework requirements for a year are listed?
options: In the Format of Assessments document for the Applied Knowledge Tests
In section 4 of the Equality Act 2010
In the learning outcomes section of each module's catalogue entry
questions.why: The Mark Scheme says students must fulfil the portfolio and coursework requirements on the Year Moodle sites. The Toolkit's catalogue entry has no learning outcomes section, so nothing is listed there. The Format of Assessments document describes the Applied Knowledge Tests and formative papers rather than portfolio items. The Equality Act 2010 is legislation on discrimination and has nothing to do with where university requirements are published.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the nine protected characteristics named in section 4 of the Equality Act 2010?
questions.why: Household income is not a protected characteristic in the Act, although income and social circumstances can still affect people's health and opportunities. Religion or belief, marriage and civil partnership, and sexual orientation are all named in section 4, along with age, disability, gender reassignment, pregnancy and maternity, race and sex.
